verdict.line: You lose if you feed Fiora Riposte punishes and let fights drag into her Duelist sustain; you win if you land E-mark into Q resets and end trades before her passive stacks up.

brief.thesis: This is a spell-timing duel between two melee ADs with a defensive W each: Fiora's Riposte (10/9/8/7/6s CD) parries basic attacks, but Irelia's Q (Bladesurge) is a spell-strike, not an auto, so it goes through Riposte clean. The matchup swings on whether Irelia opens with E (Flawless Duet) to stun and Mark before Q, or throws autos into an active Riposte and eats a reflected hit while Fiora's Duelist passive quietly stacks health back.

theirWindow.when: Riposte is up and you're about to auto
theirWindow.what: Do not walk a raw basic attack into her while Riposte is active — it gets parried and reflected as magic damage, and you lose the trade tempo. Wait out the 10/9/8/7/6s window or force it with something that isn't a basic attack.

yourWindow.when: Her Lunge is on cooldown after both charges
yourWindow.what: Fiora's Q dashes twice within a couple seconds for free, then is fully locked out for 16/14/12/10/8s. The moment you see both dashes used, engage with E (Flawless Duet) for the stun and Mark, then Q — since the target is Marked, Bladesurge's cooldown refreshes on hit, letting you chain another Q for extra damage and healing.

start.why: Run in 47.9% of 424 tracked games (86% pick rate). The extra AD and HP buys you room to eat a Lunge poke or a parried auto without losing the lane outright.

boots.why: Picked in 88.6% of games at 47.8% win rate. Fiora's damage is entirely physical autos and Lunge — Steelcaps directly cuts the poke that chips you down between all-ins.

core.why: First item in every measured core path; the on-hit percent-health damage punishes Fiora's healthy Duelist regen instead of racing raw burst.
Second item across all three tracked builds; scales your split-push and 1v1 diving power once you're ahead on the Q-E loop.
This exact path (BoRK > Hullbreaker > Wit's End) measured the highest win rate of the three core builds at 56.7% over 60 games — the attack speed feeds Ionian Fervor stacks faster.

situational.when: she's landing clean Lunge-auto trades and you need to survive the return damage from prolonged fights
you want the highest-measured alternate path (BoRK > Kraken Slayer > Death's Dance, 55.8% over 43 games) for a more front-loaded burst spike
her Duelist healing is keeping her alive through your all-ins and you need the grievous wounds

runes.keystoneWhy: The Resolve-secondary page (Conqueror, Triumph, Legend: Alacrity, Last Stand / Unflinching, Bone Plating) measured 57% win rate over the tracked sample, notably higher than the Inspiration variant — Bone Plating specifically blunts the Lunge-auto burst Fiora leans on to punish your engages.

summoners.why: The top measured combo at 47.8% win rate and 91.2% pick rate. Ignite matters specifically here — Fiora's Duelist passive heals her back through extended trades, and the burn shuts that regen off exactly when you're trying to close out a fight.

playing.title: Engage with E, not autos
playing.detail: Riposte only parries basic attacks. Open trades with E (Flawless Duet) for the stun and Mark, then follow with Q — the dash-strike is a spell hit and goes through Riposte untouched.

playing.title: Chain Q off the E Mark
playing.detail: Bladesurge's cooldown refreshes if the target is Marked or dies. Landing E right before Q means you can immediately Q again for extra damage, healing, and mobility.

playing.title: Hold autos until Riposte is confirmed down
playing.detail: Track her Riposte cooldown (10/9/8/7/6s by rank). A raw auto into an active Riposte wastes the hit and reflects magic damage back at you for free.

playing.title: Charge W into her all-in
playing.detail: Defiant Dance deals more damage the longer it charges and reduces the physical damage you take while charging — hold it as your answer to a Lunge-into-auto sequence.

playing.title: End fights fast, don't marathon
playing.detail: Her Duelist passive stacks healing every time she lands damage on you. Short, decisive trades favor you; long extended skirmishes let her regen back what you took.

playing.title: Respect first-hit burst from her R
playing.detail: Blade Waltz deals less damage on successive strikes against the same target, so a single-target duel isn't as scary as it looks — but the first hit at level 6+ still lands hard, so don't fight her ult cooldown blind.

brief.patchCaveat: Item paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade-timing advice are my own read of the ability interactions.

stats.opponentTip: Be caution of being hit with Fiora’s Reposte (W). Use [E] to engage when Irelia has 4 stacks [P] prepared while keeing her Reposte and Vitals in mind.
